title: DOMESTIC INCIDENT ARREST
full_story:
On Thursday at approximately 12:05 pm, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office was dispatched to the 5000 block of Ridge Road for a report of an active domestic violence incident.

When deputies arrived, they met with the parties involved, collected statements and evidence at the scene.  After doing so, deputies believed that the suspect had committed the offense of domestic battery.  When deputies attempted to take the suspect into custody, he attempted to flee from the deputies into his camper.  When one of the deputies grabbed the suspect trying to prevent him from getting in the camper, the suspect slammed the door on the deputy’s arm, cutting his arm.  The suspect continued to resist, which resulted in one of the deputies deploying his Taser in order to gain compliance from the suspect.

The suspect was secured in a squad car and transported to the jail.  The deputy did not require any medical attention and finished the remainder of his shift.

As a result of this incident Eric Vaultonberg, 50, of Edgewood, was arrested for the offenses of Aggravated Domestic Battery, Aggravated Battery to a Peace Officer and Resisting a Peace Officer (resulting in injury).  Vaultonberg appeared in Clay County Court Friday and was denied pretrial release.

The charge is merely an accusation and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: BREAKFAST BITES AND BUSINESS
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is sponsoring a Social Media Workshop titled Breakfast Bites and Business Insights on Wednesday.

This session, presented in partnership with America’s SBDC Illinois and Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Business & Industry, will focus on how to effectively use social media to benefit and grow your business. Participants will enjoy light breakfast bites while gaining valuable insights from the featured speaker, Chris Forde, Program Director of Marketing and Communications for IECC.  Participants will learn practical tips, strategies, and tools to strengthen your online presence and better connect with your audience.

Whether you’re just getting started or looking to improve your current social media efforts, this workshop is designed to help your business shine online.  The workshop is free for Chamber Members and $5 for non members and will start at 8:30 am on Wednesday March 25th.  Space is limited RSVP today: https://forms.gle/Z46Cs5MCa1izi3ZYA

title: FLORA LIBRARY PROGRAMS
full_story:
On Thursday, March 26th Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs’ staff will be at the Flora Public Library to help reunite citizens with missing money and property through the I-Cash program.

In Clay County, an estimated 16,600 people and/or businesses have unclaimed cash or property.  The value exceeds $1,695,000.00.  Statewide, Frerichs secures more than $5 billion in unclaimed cash and property.  The event will be from 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm on Thursday, March 26th at the Flora Public Library.

In Illinois, the state treasurer is tasked with safeguarding missing money, such as unpaid life insurance benefits, forgotten bank accounts and unused rebate cards.  Illinois holds more than $5 billion in unclaimed property.  The state treasurer is legally required to return the property to the rightful owners no matter how long it takes.  Individuals can search the state treasurer’s database for their name or the name of their business or non-profit at illinoistreasurer.gov/icash.

title: ISP OREPS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Troop 9 Commander, Lieutenant Bruce Waggoner, announced that the ISP will conduct Occupant Restraint Enforcement Patrols (OREP) in Clay and Wayne counties during April.  OREPs allow the ISP to focus on safety belts and child safety seat laws. Illinois law requires all vehicle passengers, front and back, to be buckled up.

Safety belts are still one of the most effective safety devices in vehicles, estimated to save over 14,000 lives each year.  Nearly 50% of vehicle occupants killed in traffic crashes were not buckled up.  The objective of this program is to increase occupant restraint compliance through education, child safety seat inspections, and enforcement.

title: PRETRIAL RELEASE DENIED
full_story:
Cumberland County Judge Jonathan T. Braden denied pretrial release for Darren Hays, the former White County jailer accused of having unlawful sexual contact with first-degree murder suspect Megan Valentine.  Judge Braden was appointed to hear the case after White County Resident Judge T. Scott Webb recused himself.  Judge Braden made the ruling Thursday during a detention hearing.  Pending any successful appeal, Hays will remain in the Saline County jail at Harrisburg pending trial on six counts of custodial criminal sexual misconduct with penetration and one count of official misconduct by a person of authority.

All seven charges are Class-3 felonies punishable by a maximum sentence of five years each.  A preliminary hearing for Hays has been set for Thursday, March 26 in White County Circuit Court.

title: EFFINGHAM COUNTY FAIR
full_story:
The Effingham County Fair Board announced the 2026 Grandstand Entertainment schedule, featuring a dynamic mix of events: Pro Pulling League action, a talent show, ITPA pull, queen pageant, rodeo, demolition derby, and live music.

Headlining Friday night’s concert is the legendary Jo Dee Messina.  With nine No. 1 hits, sixteen Top 40 tracks, and over five million albums sold globally, Jo Dee’s star power is undeniable.  She’s earned top honors from the ACMs, CMAs, and Grammys, promising a show packed with chart-topping music and electrifying energy.

Kicking off the show is rising country artist Cole Goodwin.  At just 24, Cole has made a name for himself with his powerful voice, heartfelt songwriting, and classic country style.  Since debuting his self-produced EP Soon Enough in 2023, he’s shared the stage with stars like Zach Top and Billy Currington, and captivated fans with singles “When You Get Home” and “Catchin’ On.”  Recognized as Savannah’s Best Country Artist in both 2023 and 2024, Cole recently joined the Big Machine Records roster.

The concert happens at the Effingham County Fairgrounds in Altamont, on August 7th.  Gates open at 6 PM, and the music starts at 7:30 PM.  Tickets for all grandstand events are on sale now, visit effinghamcountyfair.com for more details and show information.

title: SPRING TROUT SEASON
full_story:
The 2026 Illinois spring trout fishing season will open Saturday, April 4th at 58 ponds, lakes, and streams throughout the state.

An early opportunity at select trout sites, the spring catch-and-release fishing season, is now open.  No trout may be kept during the catch-and-release period, but anglers can keep trout after the opening of the regular season beginning April 4th.  The daily harvest limit for each angler is five trout.

Trout Fishing can be done at the Sam Dale Lake State Fish and Wildlife Area in Wayne County, at the Turkey Run Shelter Pond, because the trout pond continues to undergo rehabilitation.  Signs directing anglers to the temporary site will be posted.  At the Mount Vernon Game Farm Pond in Jefferson County, or at the Beall Woods Lake, at the Beall Woods State Park, in Wabash County, and the Boston Pond, at the Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County.

For information about all site regulations, anglers should contact individual sites that will be stocked with catchable-size trout.  Not all sites are open for trout catch-and-release season and not all sites are open at 5 am opening day.

The Illinois Catchable Trout Program receives funding support by those who use the program through the sale of inland trout stamps.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources stocks more than 80,000 rainbow trout each year in bodies of water where trout fishing is permitted during the spring season.  An additional 80,000 trout will be stocked for the fall trout season, which begins in October.

The spring trout season offers opportunities for families to get outdoors and enjoy fishing.  All anglers must have a fishing license and an inland trout stamp unless they are younger than 16, blind or disabled, or are an Illinois resident on leave from active duty in the Armed Forces.

Fishing licenses and trout stamps can be purchased by using a credit card online.  Visit ifishillinois.org for more information on trout seasons and other Illinois fishing opportunities.

title: LARGE-CAPACITY MAGAZINE BAN STRUCK DOWN
full_story:
A recent decision from a local appellate court in Washington, DC, striking down a ban on large-capacity magazines could have an impact on a pending case challenging a similar ban in Illinois.

In a memo filed March 11th with the 7th US Circuit Court of Appeals in Chicago, lawyers for the gun industry asked a three-judge panel hearing the Illinois challenge to consider the case of Tyree Benson.  His conviction for violating a local ordinance banning large-capacity magazines was recently overturned by the Washington, DC, Court of Appeals on Second Amendment grounds.

But Attorney General Kwame Raoul’s office responded Wednesday, arguing the 7th Circuit is not bound by decisions of the DC court, the equivalent of a state supreme court.  It also described the Benson decision as an “outlier that conflicts with every other appellate court to have addressed the issue.”

At issue before the 7th Circuit is a constitutional challenge to the Protect Illinois Communities Act, or PICA, a sweeping ban on assault-style weapons and large-capacity magazines.

Illinois lawmakers passed that ban during a lame duck session in January 2023 following a mass shooting the previous summer at a Fourth of July parade in Highland Park that left seven people dead and dozens more injured or traumatized. The convicted gunman in that shooting used a Smith & Wesson M&P15 semiautomatic rifle and multiple 30-round magazines.

In November 2024, a federal judge in East St. Louis sided with gun rights advocates and the gun industry and struck down the Illinois law as unconstitutional.  The state appealed that decision to the 7th Circuit, which heard oral arguments in September but has not yet rendered a decision.  The law remains in effect while the appeal is pending.

Many legal observers say the case is likely to end up before the US Supreme Court, which has never issued a definitive ruling on assault weapons bans.  The court did, however, deny requests to issue preliminary injunctions blocking the law from being enforced while legal challenges proceeded.
